newsitem.title: USA: Judge will lift stay for Marvel bondholders.
newsitem.headline: Judge will lift stay for Marvel bondholders.

text.p: U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Helen Balick ruled on Tuesday to remove an automatic stay that prevents bondholders of Marvel Entertainment Inc's parent company from attempting to foreclose on common stock that collateralizes their bonds.

Bondholder attorney David Friedman said the ruling gives bondholders the right to vote to foreclose on the stock "without limitations." The bondholders will now consider whether to excercise that right, he said.

"We've been granted the opportunity to vote...but we hope that won't be necessary," Friedman said. "We hope to sit down with the Marvel board and convince them that that the current plan on file is not in the best interest of any party."
Bondholders have been fighting a Chapter 11 reorganization plan of majority investor Ronald Perelman that would reimburse them $0.045 on the dollar in return for the stock.

Perelman's plan is based on a series of deals that begin with a $365 million equity investment in Marvel from his wholly-owned Andrews Group Inc. The money would be earmarked to buy Toy Biz Inc stock not already owned by Marvel.
Perelman would then control 80 percent of new Marvel stock while bondholders' collateral would be diluted from 78.8 percent to 17.2 percent.
Marvel spokesman Michael Freitag said the company will review the available legal options, including an appeal or request for a temporary restraining order.
Balick said arguments presented by Marvel's parent company against the bondholders request were without merit.
